notes: The tax is figured on the price or the J.D. Power clean trade-in value, whichever is greater. If you think your vehicle is worth less, the DMV has an appraisal form that can lower the tax.

content.intro: {state} charges a {stateRate} purchase and use tax when you title a vehicle, figured on the price after your trade-in. The tax uses the higher of the price or the vehicle's book value.

howItWorks.text: The tax is {stateRate} of the purchase price or the J.D. Power clean trade-in value, whichever is greater. The value of a trade-in comes off before the tax is figured.
If you think the book value is higher than what the vehicle is worth, you can ask the DMV for a lower tax with an appraisal form at registration.
Registration is paid yearly or for two years, and the fee depends on the fuel type. Battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles also pay an infrastructure fee.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the tax in Vermont?
faq.text: Yes. The instructions subtract the value of any trade-in vehicle or other allowable credit from the price before the tax is figured.

faq.q: Why can the tax be higher than the price I paid?
faq.text: Vermont taxes the higher of the purchase price or the J.D. Power clean trade-in value. A very low price does not lower the tax below the book value.

faq.q: Do electric vehicles pay more to register?
faq.text: Yes. A battery electric vehicle has a higher registration fee than a gas vehicle and also pays an infrastructure fee.
